subproblem.title: Linear algebra of graph planes: (Gp), (Nor), norm comparison, rotations, continuity
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1 and l >= 0 there is L_0 = L_0(n,l) in (0, 1/4] such that, writing P_q(A) for the orthogonal projection of R^(n+l) onto q(graph A) = (span{graphPoint v (A v)}).map q (A : R^n -> R^l linear, q a linear isometry of R^(n+l)), |.| for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm and ||.|| for the operator norm: (1) if |A|, |B| <= L_0 then |A - B|^2 <= |P_q(A) - P_q(B)|^2 <= 3|A - B|^2; (2) if |A| <= L_0 then |A|^2 <= |P_q(A) - p_{rotatedPlane q}|^2; (3) if ||A|| <= 1 then |y - A x| <= 2 |w - P_q(A) w| for w = q(graphPoint x y), all x in R^n, y in R^l; (4) ||A|| <= |A| <= sqrt(n) ||A||; (5) every n-dimensional subspace T equals rotatedPlane q for some linear isometry q; (6) A -> P_q(A) is continuous.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∃ L₀ : ℝ, 0 < L₀ ∧ L₀ ≤ 1 / 4 ∧ (∀ (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (A B : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), hsNorm A ≤ L₀ → hsNorm B ≤ L₀ → hsNormSq (A - B) ≤ hsNormSq (((Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap).starProjection - ((Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (B v))).map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap).starProjection) ∧ hsNormSq (((Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap).starProjection - ((Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (B v))).map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap).starProjection) ≤ 3 * hsNormSq (A - B)) ∧ (∀ (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), hsNorm A ≤ L₀ → hsNormSq A ≤ hsNormSq (((Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap).starProjection - (rotatedPlane q).starProjection)) ∧ (∀ (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (x : Rn n) (y : Rn ℓ), ‖A‖ ≤ 1 → ‖y - A x‖ ≤ 2 * ‖q (graphPoint x y) - ((Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap).starProjection (q (graphPoint x y))‖) ∧ (∀ A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, ‖A‖ ≤ hsNorm A ∧ hsNorm A ≤ Real.sqrt n * ‖A‖) ∧ (∀ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ T = n → ∃ q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ, rotatedPlane q = T) ∧ (∀ q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ, Continuous fun A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => ((Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap).starProjection)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the facts (Gp) and (Nor) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 5, proof of 5.2, the estimate before (11)), together with three elementary facts the parent proof uses implicitly (the norm comparison ||A|| <= |A| <= sqrt(n) ||A||, the existence of a linear isometry q with rotatedPlane q = T, and continuity of the graph projection).

Notation. For a linear map A : R^n -> R^l let J_A : R^n -> R^(n+l), J_A v := graphPoint v (A v); J_A is linear and injective, J_A^* J_A = I + A^* A (invertible), and Gamma_A := range J_A = span{graphPoint v (A v)} is n-dimensional. Pi(A) := orthogonal projection onto Gamma_A = J_A (I + A^* A)^-1 J_A^*; in block form with respect to R^n x R^l,
 Pi(A) = [[(I + A^*A)^-1, (I + A^*A)^-1 A^*], [A (I + A^*A)^-1, A (I + A^*A)^-1 A^*]].
For a linear isometry q of R^(n+l), the subspace (span{graphPoint v (A v)}).map q is q(Gamma_A) and its orthogonal projection (starProjection) is P_q(A) = q Pi(A) q^-1. |X| denotes the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm; |X|^2 = hsNormSq X = trace(X^* X), independent of the orthonormal basis), ||X|| the operator norm. Conjugation by a linear isometry preserves |.|.

1. Continuity (last conjunct). A -> I + A^*A is continuous with values in the invertible operators, inversion is continuous there, and composition/adjoint are continuous; hence A -> Pi(A) and A -> P_q(A) = q Pi(A) q^-1 are continuous (in fact real analytic) on the space of linear maps R^n -> R^l.

2. Derivative at 0. Differentiating Pi(tH) = J_{tH}(I + t^2 H^*H)^-1 J_{tH}^* at t = 0 gives DPi(0)[H] = [[0, H^*], [H, 0]], so |DPi(0)[H]|^2 = |H^*|^2 + |H|^2 = 2|H|^2.

3. (Gp) (first conjunct). Pi is C^infinity, so C_g := 1 + sup_{|X| <= 1} ||D^2 Pi(X)|| < infinity (norms built from |.|; compactness of the unit ball of the finite-dimensional space of linear maps), and ||DPi(X) - DPi(0)|| <= C_g |X| for |X| <= 1. Put L_0 := min{1/4, (sqrt 3 - sqrt 2)/C_g}; it depends only on n, l, and 0 < L_0 <= 1/4. If |A|, |B| <= L_0, the segment from B to A lies in {|X| <= L_0}, so by the mean value inequality |Pi(A) - Pi(B) - DPi(0)[A - B]| <= C_g L_0 |A - B|. With step 2,
 (sqrt 2 - C_g L_0)|A - B| <= |Pi(A) - Pi(B)| <= (sqrt 2 + C_g L_0)|A - B|.
 Since C_g L_0 <= sqrt 3 - sqrt 2, we have sqrt 2 - C_g L_0 >= 2 sqrt 2 - sqrt 3 > 1 and sqrt 2 + C_g L_0 <= sqrt 3, so |A - B|^2 <= |Pi(A) - Pi(B)|^2 <= 3 |A - B|^2. As |P_q(A) - P_q(B)| = |q (Pi(A) - Pi(B)) q^-1| = |Pi(A) - Pi(B)|, this is the first conjunct: hsNormSq(A - B) <= hsNormSq(P_q(A) - P_q(B)) <= 3 hsNormSq(A - B).

4. The case B = 0 (second conjunct). graphPoint v 0 = sum_{i<n} v_i e_{castAdd i}, so Gamma_0 = span{e_{castAdd i} : i < n} = horizontalPlane n l and q(Gamma_0) = rotatedPlane q. Applying step 3 with B = 0 (|0| = 0 <= L_0) gives hsNormSq A <= hsNormSq(P_q(A) - (rotatedPlane q).starProjection) whenever |A| <= L_0.

5. (Nor) (third conjunct). Let x in R^n, y in R^l, w := q(graphPoint x y). Then |w - P_q(A)w| = dist(w, q(Gamma_A)) = dist(graphPoint x y, Gamma_A) = inf_v |graphPoint (x - v) (y - A v)|. For every v, |y - A x| <= |y - A v| + |A(v - x)| <= |y - A v| + ||A|| |x - v| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) (|y - Av|^2 + |x - v|^2)^(1/2) (Cauchy-Schwarz) = (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) |graphPoint (x - v) (y - Av)|. Taking the infimum, |y - A x| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) |w - P_q(A) w| <= sqrt 2 |w - P_q(A) w| <= 2 |w - P_q(A) w| when ||A|| <= 1.

6. Norm comparison (fourth conjunct). For a unit vector u = sum u_i e_i, |A u| <= sum |u_i| |A e_i| <= (sum u_i^2)^(1/2)(sum |A e_i|^2)^(1/2) = |A|, so ||A|| <= |A| = hsNorm A; and hsNormSq A = sum_{i<n} |A e_i|^2 <= n ||A||^2, so hsNorm A <= sqrt(n) ||A||.

7. Rotations (fifth conjunct). Let T be a subspace with dim T = n. Choose an orthonormal basis u_0, ..., u_{n-1} of T and an orthonormal basis u_n, ..., u_{n+l-1} of T^perp (dim T^perp = l). The linear map q with q(e_{castAdd i}) = u_i (i < n) and q(e_{natAdd n j}) = u_{n+j} (j < l) sends an orthonormal basis to an orthonormal basis, hence is a linear isometry equivalence of R^(n+l), and rotatedPlane q = q(span{e_{castAdd i}}) = span{u_0, ..., u_{n-1}} = T.

Steps 1-7 prove all six conjuncts, with L_0 = L_0(n, l) in (0, 1/4].
proof_key_steps: Write P_q(A) = q Pi(A) q^-1 with Pi(A) = J_A (I + A^*A)^-1 J_A^*, continuous and smooth
DPi(0)[H] = [[0, H^*],[H, 0]] has Hilbert-Schmidt norm sqrt(2)|H|
Mean value inequality with C_g L_0 <= sqrt 3 - sqrt 2 gives the two-sided comparison
graph 0 is the horizontal plane, so B = 0 gives the comparison with rotatedPlane q
Distance to graph A bounds |y - Ax| by Cauchy-Schwarz
Norm comparison and rotations from orthonormal bases

subproblem.title: Radial integration: small conical excess of a C^1 graph bounds its height
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l >= 0, alpha in (0,1], M >= 0 and A >= 0 there is C >= 0 such that: if R > 0, 0 < delta <= 1, f : R^n -> R^l with f(0) = 0, f C^1 and 1-Lipschitz on the open ball B^o_R(0), hsNorm(Df(x)) <= M (|x|/R)^alpha for x in B^o_R(0), and the extended integral over B^o_R(0) of |f(x) - Df(x) x|^2 |x|^(-n-2) dx is at most A delta, then |f(x)| <= C delta^(1/(2n+2)) |x| for every x in B^o_R(0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (α M A : ℝ), 0 < α → α ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ M → 0 ≤ A → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (R δ : ℝ), 0 < R → 0 < δ → δ ≤ 1 → f 0 = 0 → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball 0 R) → LipschitzOnWith 1 f (ball 0 R) → (∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) R, hsNorm (fderiv ℝ f x) ≤ M * (‖x‖ / R) ^ α) → ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Rn n) R, ENNReal.ofReal (‖f x - fderiv ℝ f x x‖ ^ 2 / ‖x‖ ^ (n + 2)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (A * δ) → ∀ x ∈ ball (0 : Rn n) R, ‖f x‖ ≤ C * δ ^ (1 / (2 * (n : ℝ) + 2)) * ‖x‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the radial-integration argument in step 6 of the parent proof (Part III, not in the printed text), isolated as a statement about functions on R^n.

Notation. a := 1/(2n+2); S := S^(n-1), the unit sphere of R^n; |.| Euclidean norms, ||.|| the operator norm, hsNorm the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (||B|| <= hsNorm B).
Facts used. (Pol) Polar coordinates (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.toSphere and measurePreserving_homeomorphUnitSphereProd): there is a finite Borel measure sigma on S such that integral_{R^n} g dL^n = integral_S integral_0^infinity g(t w) t^(n-1) dt dsigma(w) for every Borel g >= 0, and sigma(A) = n L^n({t w : 0 < t < 1, w in A}). For n = 1, S = {-1, 1} and sigma is counting measure. (Cap) For n >= 2 there is c_n > 0 with sigma(S cap B_tau(w_0)) >= c_n tau^(n-1) for w_0 in S and 0 < tau <= 1: with w_0 = e_1, the box Q := {x : x_1 in [1/2, 3/4], |(x_2,...,x_n)| <= tau/4} lies in {t w : 1/2 <= t <= 1, w in S cap B_tau(w_0)} (for x in Q, 1/2 <= |x| <= 1 and |x/|x| - e_1| <= 2|(x_2,...,x_n)|/|x| <= tau), so L^n(Q) = (1/4) omega_{n-1} (tau/4)^(n-1) <= sigma(S cap B_tau(w_0)) integral_{1/2}^1 t^(n-1) dt <= sigma(S cap B_tau(w_0))/n.
Constants. Given n >= 1, alpha in (0,1], M >= 0, A >= 0: put c_1 := 1, K_n := (4^n A/(c_n alpha))^(1/(n+1)) and C := M + K_n >= 0.

Let f, R, delta satisfy the hypotheses: 0 < R, 0 < delta <= 1, f(0) = 0, f in C^1 on B^o_R(0), f 1-Lipschitz on B^o_R(0), hsNorm(Df(x)) <= M (|x|/R)^alpha on B^o_R(0), and integral_{B^o_R(0)} |f(x) - Df(x)x|^2 |x|^(-n-2) dx <= A delta.

1. Basic bounds. |f(x)| = |f(x) - f(0)| <= |x| on B^o_R(0), and ||Df(x)|| <= hsNorm(Df(x)) <= M (|x|/R)^alpha.

2. Radial quotient. For w in S and 0 < t < R put W(t, w) := f(t w)/t. W is C^1 in t with d/dt W(t, w) = (Df(t w)(t w) - f(t w))/t^2, hence t |d/dt W(t, w)|^2 = |f(t w) - Df(t w)(t w)|^2 t^-3 = g(t w) t^(n-1) with g(x) := |f(x) - Df(x)x|^2 |x|^(-n-2) (a nonnegative Borel function on B^o_R(0) minus {0}). By (Pol),
 integral_S integral_0^R t |d/dt W(t, w)|^2 dt dsigma(w) = integral_{B^o_R(0)} g dL^n <= A delta.

3. Small radii. Put r_1 := delta^(1/alpha) R in (0, R]. For 0 < t <= r_1 and w in S, the mean value inequality on the segment [0, t w] and step 1 give |W(t, w)| = |f(t w) - f(0)|/t <= sup_{|x| <= t} ||Df(x)|| <= M (t/R)^alpha <= M (r_1/R)^alpha = M delta.

4. L^2 bound on the sphere. For r_1 <= r < R and w in S let D_r(w) := W(r, w) - W(r_1, w) = integral_{r_1}^r d/dt W(t, w) dt. By Cauchy-Schwarz, |D_r(w)|^2 <= (integral_{r_1}^r dt/t)(integral_{r_1}^r t |d/dt W|^2 dt) <= log(R/r_1) integral_0^R t |d/dt W(t, w)|^2 dt. Integrating over S (Tonelli) and using step 2 and log(R/r_1) = alpha^-1 log(1/delta):
 integral_S |D_r|^2 dsigma <= (A/alpha) delta log(1/delta).

5. From L^2 to sup. Since f is 1-Lipschitz, |W(t, w) - W(t, w')| = |f(t w) - f(t w')|/t <= |w - w'|, so D_r is 2-Lipschitz on S; and |W| <= 1 by step 1, so |D_r| <= 2. Let w_0 in S and m := |D_r(w_0)| (<= 2).
 If n >= 2: for w in S cap B_{m/4}(w_0), |D_r(w)| >= m - 2(m/4) = m/2, and m/4 <= 1/2, so by (Cap) integral_S |D_r|^2 dsigma >= (m/2)^2 c_n (m/4)^(n-1) = c_n 4^-n m^(n+1).
 If n = 1: S = {-1, 1} with counting measure, so integral_S |D_r|^2 dsigma >= |D_r(w_0)|^2 = m^2 = m^(n+1) >= c_1 4^-n m^(n+1).
 In both cases, by step 4, m <= (4^n (A/alpha) delta log(1/delta)/c_n)^(1/(n+1)) = K_n (delta log(1/delta))^(1/(n+1)).

6. Removing the logarithm. (delta log(1/delta))^(1/(n+1)) = delta^(2a) (log(1/delta))^(2a) = delta^a (delta^(1/2) log(1/delta))^(2a) <= delta^a, because sup_{0 < delta <= 1} delta^(1/2) log(1/delta) = 2/e < 1. Also delta <= delta^a since 0 < delta <= 1 and a < 1.

7. Conclusion. Let x in B^o_R(0). If x = 0 then |f(x)| = 0. Otherwise write x = r w with r = |x| in (0, R), w in S. If r <= r_1, step 3 gives |f(x)| = r |W(r, w)| <= M delta r <= M delta^a |x|. If r_1 < r < R, steps 3, 5 and 6 give |f(x)| = r |W(r, w)| <= r (|W(r_1, w)| + |D_r(w)|) <= r (M delta + K_n delta^a) <= (M + K_n) delta^a |x|. Hence ||f x|| <= C delta^(1/(2n+2)) ||x|| for every x in ball 0 R, with C = M + K_n depending only on n, alpha, M, A.
proof_key_steps: Polar coordinates turn the weighted integral into integral_S integral_0^R t |d/dt (f(tw)/t)|^2 dt dsigma
Small radii r <= r_1 = delta^(1/alpha) R: |f(tw)|/t <= M delta
Cauchy-Schwarz in t bounds the sphere L^2 norm of the increment by (A/alpha) delta log(1/delta)
Lipschitz continuity on the sphere converts the L^2 bound into a sup bound via spherical caps
(delta log(1/delta))^(1/(n+1)) <= delta^(1/(2n+2))

subproblem.title: Tangent planes exist a.e., are measurable, and density = multiplicity a.e. (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6-1.9)
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, U an open subset of R^(n+l), and V a rectifiable n-varifold in U in the sense of the contract (carrier M contained in U, H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable; multiplicity theta positive on M, H^n-a.e.-measurable on M and H^n-integrable on M cap K for each compact K contained in U), mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M. Then: (i) x -> V.tangentProj x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (ii) for mu-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional subspace P with V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection (the approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta, Simon Ch. 3, 1.7, exists at mu-a.e. x); (iii) for mu-a.e. x, V.HasDensity x (V.mult x), i.e. mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x) as r -> 0+.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U, AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n ∧ V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, V.HasDensity x (V.mult x))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 3, Def. 1.4, 1.7, Lemma 1.2, Rem. 1.3, Thm. 1.6 ('=>'), Rem. 1.8(1),(2), Thm. 1.9 (the fact (F1) of the parent proof), with the measurability step made explicit.

Notation. M := V.carrier (a subset of U), theta := V.mult, mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (theta := 0 off M), p_x := V.tangentProj x, eta_{x,r}(w) := (w - x)/r, B_r(x) the closed ball, B^o_r(x) the open ball, omega_n := unitBallVolume n; for an n-dimensional subspace P, p_P := P.starProjection. Hypotheses: U open; M is H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable; theta > 0 on M, theta is H^n-a.e.-measurable on M, and theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K for every compact K contained in U.

1. Two reductions.
 (a) mu(R^(n+l) minus M) = 0, and a set N contained in M is mu-null iff it is H^n-null: if H^n(N) = 0 then mu(N) = 0; conversely, if mu(N) = 0 take an H^n-measurable N' containing N with mu(N' cap M) = 0 (measurable hull); then integral_{N' cap M} theta dH^n = 0 with theta > 0 on M forces H^n(N' cap M) = 0. Hence (ii) and (iii) follow once they are proved at H^n-a.e. x in M, and (i) follows once p is shown to be a mu-a.e. limit of Borel maps.
 (b) [Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7 = SimonGMT Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt, the predicate used to define tangentProj] An n-dimensional subspace P is an approximate tangent space of M w.r.t. theta at x if lim_{r -> 0+} integral_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f(z) theta(x + r z) dH^n(z) = theta(x) integral_P f dH^n for every f in C_c(R^(n+l)). Since H^n(x + r E) = r^n H^n(E), for x in U and r so small that x + r spt f is a compact subset of U,
 (*) integral_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f(z) theta(x + r z) dH^n(z) = r^-n integral_M f((w - x)/r) theta(w) dH^n(w) = r^-n integral f((w - x)/r) dmu(w),
 and this integral is finite because theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K for compact K in U. If x in M then theta(x) > 0, so such a P is unique (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), and by the definition of tangentProj, p_x = p_P whenever such a P exists; then dim P = n.

2. Localization. Let U_k := {x : |x| < k and B_{1/k}(x) is contained in U} (closed balls; this avoids distances to a possibly empty complement). U_k is open (if B_{1/k}(x) is contained in U then, by compactness, so is B_{1/k + eps}(x) for some eps > 0), its closure is a compact subset of U (if x_m -> x with B_{1/k}(x_m) in U then B^o_{1/k}(x) is contained in U, so x in U, and the closure is bounded), and U = union_k U_k (U is open). Put M_k := M cap U_k: it is H^n-measurable, countably n-rectifiable (a subset of M) and integral_{M_k cap K} theta dH^n < infinity for every compact K in R^(n+l). If x in M_k, spt f is contained in B_rho'(0) and r rho' is so small that B_{r rho'}(x) is contained in U_k (possible since U_k is open), then f((w - x)/r) != 0 implies w in U_k, so the integrals (*) for (M, theta) and for (M_k, theta) coincide; hence the approximate tangent spaces of (M, theta) and (M_k, theta) at x coincide (existence and value), and mu(B_r(x)) = (theta H^n restricted to M_k)(B_r(x)) for small r. As M = union_k M_k, it suffices to prove (ii) and (iii) at H^n-a.e. point of each M_k for the pair (M_k, theta), which satisfies the global hypotheses of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7-1.9. In steps 3 and 4 we therefore assume integral_{M cap K} theta dH^n < infinity for every compact K, so that mu is a Radon measure on R^(n+l).

3. Existence of T_x(M, theta) for H^n-a.e. x in M (Simon Ch. 3, Thm. 1.9).
 (a) [Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Rem. 1.3] Since M is countably n-rectifiable there are an H^n-null set N_0 and embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifolds N_1, N_2, ... of R^(n+l) with M contained in union_{j >= 0} N_j. (Proof of Lemma 1.2: M is contained in N'_0 union union_i F_i(R^n) with H^n(N'_0) = 0 and F_i Lipschitz; by the C^1 approximation theorem (Ch. 2, 1.5; its Whitney-extension core is SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney) each F_i coincides, outside sets of arbitrarily small L^n-measure, with C^1 maps G_ij; by the area formula G_ij({J G_ij = 0}) is H^n-null, and each point of {J G_ij != 0} has a neighbourhood whose G_ij-image is an embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifold (inverse function theorem); countably many such neighbourhoods suffice.) The cover can be disjointified into H^n-measurable pieces (SimonGMT Chapter03.simon_remark_1_3).
 (b) [Ch. 3, Rem. 1.8(1)] H^n restricted to M is sigma-finite (H^n(M cap K cap {theta > 1/j}) <= j integral_{M cap K} theta). By Lusin's theorem there are compact sets K_1, K_2, ... contained in M, increasing, with H^n(M minus union_i K_i) = 0 and theta restricted to K_i continuous; theta has a positive minimum c_i on K_i, so H^n(K_i) <= c_i^-1 integral_{K_i} theta < infinity. By the upper density theorem (Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6) applied to the Radon measure mu restricted to (M minus K_i), there is an H^n-null set E_i such that r^-n mu(B_r(x) minus K_i) -> 0 as r -> 0 for every x in K_i minus E_i.
 (c) [Ch. 3, Thm. 1.6 '=>' for K_i] Fix i and put K_ij := K_i cap N_j minus union_{j' < j} N_j' (so H^n(K_i0) = 0). Fix j >= 1. N_j is covered by countably many open sets W in which N_j cap W is a C^1 graph of finite H^n-measure. By the upper density theorem for the finite measures H^n restricted to (K_i minus K_ij) and H^n restricted to ((N_j cap W) minus K_ij), for H^n-a.e. x in K_ij cap W both measures have zero n-dimensional density at x. Since N_j is C^1 at x, lim_{r -> 0} integral_{eta_{x,r}(N_j)} f dH^n = integral_{T_x N_j} f dH^n for f in C_c. Writing integral_{eta_{x,r}(K_i)} f = integral_{eta_{x,r}(N_j)} f - integral_{eta_{x,r}(N_j minus K_ij)} f + integral_{eta_{x,r}(K_i minus K_ij)} f and bounding the last two terms (for spt f in B_rho'(0)) by sup|f| r^-n H^n(B_{rho' r}(x) cap (N_j minus K_ij)) and sup|f| r^-n H^n(B_{rho' r}(x) cap (K_i minus K_ij)), which tend to 0, we get lim integral_{eta_{x,r}(K_i)} f dH^n = integral_{T_x N_j} f dH^n: the unweighted approximate tangent space T_x K_i (Def. 1.4) exists and equals T_x N_j. Hence T_x K_i exists for H^n-a.e. x in K_i.
 (d) [Ch. 3, Rem. 1.8(1)] Let x in K_i minus E_i be a point at which P := T_x K_i exists, and let f in C_c with spt f in B_rho'(0). By (*), integral_{eta_{x,r}(M)} f(z) theta(x + r z) dH^n(z) = r^-n integral_{K_i} f((w - x)/r) theta(w) dH^n(w) + r^-n integral_{M minus K_i} f((w - x)/r) dmu(w). The second term is at most sup|f| r^-n mu(B_{rho' r}(x) minus K_i) -> 0 by (b). In the first term |theta(w) - theta(x)| <= eps_r -> 0 uniformly for w in K_i cap B_{rho' r}(x) (continuity of theta on K_i), and r^-n H^n(K_i cap B_{rho' r}(x)) stays bounded (it converges to omega_n rho'^n by (c) applied to test functions squeezing the indicator of B_rho'(0)); hence the first term equals theta(x) integral_{eta_{x,r}(K_i)} f dH^n + o(1) -> theta(x) integral_P f dH^n. So P is the approximate tangent space of M w.r.t. theta at x.
 Since H^n(M minus union_i K_i) = 0 and every E_i is H^n-null, T_x(M, theta) exists for H^n-a.e. x in M. By 1(a),(b) this proves (ii): for mu-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional P with V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection.

4. Density (iii) (Ch. 3, Rem. 1.8(2)). Let x in M be such that P := T_x(M, theta) exists. For eps in (0,1) choose continuous compactly supported g_eps, h_eps : R^(n+l) -> [0,1] with g_eps = 1 on B_1(0), g_eps = 0 outside B_{1+eps}(0), h_eps = 1 on B_{1-eps}(0) and h_eps = 0 outside B^o_1(0). By (*), r^-n integral h_eps((w - x)/r) dmu <= r^-n mu(B_r(x)) <= r^-n integral g_eps((w - x)/r) dmu, and as r -> 0 the outer terms converge to theta(x) integral_P h_eps dH^n >= theta(x) omega_n (1 - eps)^n and to theta(x) integral_P g_eps dH^n <= theta(x) omega_n (1 + eps)^n (H^n on P is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure, H^n(P cap B_t(0)) = omega_n t^n). Letting eps -> 0, mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x) in (0, infinity); in extended reals, mu(B_r(x)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> ofReal(theta(x)) as r -> 0+, i.e. V.HasDensity x (V.mult x). By step 3 and 1(a) this holds for mu-a.e. x.

5. Measurability (i). Let phi(t) := max{0, 1 - t} (t >= 0), c_0 := integral_{R^n} phi(|t|) dt > 0 and c_1 := (1/n) integral_{R^n} phi(|t|) |t|^2 dt > 0. For an n-dimensional subspace P with orthonormal basis tau_1, ..., tau_n, the isometric parametrization t -> sum_k t_k tau_k gives integral_P phi(|z|) dH^n(z) = c_0 and integral_P phi(|z|) z (x) z dH^n(z) = sum_{k,k'} (integral phi(|t|) t_k t_k' dt) tau_k (x) tau_k' = c_1 p_P (mixed moments vanish by the symmetry t_k -> -t_k, and integral phi(|t|) t_k^2 dt = c_1 for each k). For k >= 1 let W_k := {x : B_{2/k}(x) is contained in U} (open, as in step 2; U = union_k W_k) and for x in W_k set
 a_k(x) := k^n integral phi(k |w - x|) dmu(w), b_k(x) := k^(n+2) integral phi(k |w - x|) (w - x) (x) (w - x) dmu(w)
 (b_k(x) is a linear operator on R^(n+l)). The integrands are bounded, continuous in x and supported in B_{1/k}(x); for x within 1/k of a point x_0 in W_k these balls lie in the compact set B_{2/k}(x_0), contained in U, on which mu is finite, so a_k, b_k are continuous on W_k by dominated convergence. Define h_k(x) := (c_0/c_1) b_k(x)/a_k(x) if x in W_k and a_k(x) > 0, and h_k(x) := 0 otherwise; each h_k is Borel. If x in M and P = T_x(M, theta) exists, then x in W_k for large k and, by (*) with r = 1/k and the compactly supported continuous test functions z -> phi(|z|) and z -> phi(|z|) z_i z_j, a_k(x) -> theta(x) c_0 > 0 and b_k(x) -> theta(x) c_1 p_P; hence h_k(x) -> p_P = p_x by 1(b). By step 3 this convergence holds for mu-a.e. x. So p is the mu-a.e. limit of Borel, hence strongly measurable, maps into the finite-dimensional space of operators on R^(n+l), and is therefore mu-a.e. strongly measurable (Mathlib aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae). This proves (i), and with steps 3 and 4 the theorem.
proof_key_steps: Reduce to H^n-a.e. statements on M and localize to pieces M_k on which theta is globally integrable
Cover M by C^1 submanifolds (Ch. 3, 1.2/1.3) and split by Lusin into compact pieces K_i with continuous theta
Upper density theorem gives T_x K_i = T_x N_j a.e. (Thm 1.6) and then the weighted tangent space T_x(M, theta) (Rem 1.8(1))
Squeezing test functions gives density = theta (Rem 1.8(2))
Second-moment quotients h_k are Borel and converge a.e. to p_x, so tangentProj is a.e. strongly measurable

audit.reason: The type matches all three assertions and the local hypotheses. Localization, the rectifiable-cover/Lusin argument, density squeezing, and Borel second-moment approximants establish the exact conclusions without assuming Allard regularity.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the facts (M), (M.iv) and (P) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 4.1-4.10 with the corrected coefficient kappa = (p-n)/(4p) of 4.2, and Simon Ch. 5, 2.4 with explicit constants), copied and completed. The argument is arranged so that the quantifier structure of the statement is visible: the constants delta_P and C_P are fixed in step 1 from n and p alone, before the codimension l and the data U, V, H, delta, rho, y, s are chosen (steps 2-8 work for every l with these fixed constants).

Notation. Fix n >= 1 and p > n. kappa := (p-n)/(4p) in (0, 1/4), alpha' := 1 - n/p in (0,1), omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0. From step 2 on, l >= 0 is arbitrary, U is an open subset of R^(n+l), V is a rectifiable n-varifold in U (M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult) with generalized mean curvature H, mu := V.weight, spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu, p_x := V.tangentProj x, p_x^perp := I - p_x, K(z,s) := (s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) in [0, infinity] (= V.scaledLpNorm H p z s). For a centre y put r := |x - y| and nu_y(x) := |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2 / |x - y|^2 for x != y, nu_y(y) := 0; then nu_y(x) r^-n = ||x - y - p_x(x - y)||^2 / ||x - y||^(n+2), and both sides vanish at x = y (real division by 0 is 0). Balls B_s(z) are closed.
Facts used. (T) [sibling allard52_tangent_ae, applied to n, l, U, V] p is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace; Theta^n(mu, x) = theta(x) for mu-a.e. x (V.HasDensity x (V.mult x)). (F2) mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0, mu(R^(n+l) minus U) = 0 and mu(K) < infinity for compact K in U (theta is integrable on M cap K).

1. Constants; they depend only on n and p. Let t_0 := min{1/8, kappa} and, for t in [0, t_0], Lambda_t := t/kappa in [0,1],
 g_+(t) := e^(2 Lambda_t)(1 + t)(1 - 3t)^-n + 2 e^(Lambda_t) Lambda_t/omega_n,
 g_-(t) := e^(-Lambda_t)(1 - Lambda_t/omega_n),
 g_c(t) := e^(Lambda_t)(e^(Lambda_t)(1 + t)(1 - 3t)^-n - 1) + e^(Lambda_t) Lambda_t/omega_n.
 They are C^1 on [0, t_0] (1 - 3t >= 5/8), with g_+(0) = g_-(0) = 1 and g_c(0) = 0. Let C_P := max{1, sup|g_+'|, sup|g_-'|, sup|g_c'|} (suprema over [0, t_0]); by the mean value theorem g_+(t) <= 1 + C_P t, g_-(t) >= 1 - C_P t and g_c(t) <= C_P t on [0, t_0]. Put delta_P := min{t_0, 1/(2 C_P)}. Then 0 < delta_P <= 1/8, C_P > 0 and C_P delta_P <= 1/2. Only kappa and omega_n enter, so delta_P and C_P depend only on n and p and are the same for every codimension l. From now on let l >= 0 be arbitrary; steps 2-8 prove, for this l and all U, V, H, delta, rho, y, s as in the statement, the asserted bounds with these fixed delta_P, C_P. This is exactly the statement with "there exist delta_P, C_P" placed before "for all l".

2. Curvature scaling. Under 2.3, if B_s(z) is contained in B_rho(0) then K(z,s)^p = s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p dmu <= s^(p-n) integral_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p dmu <= (s/rho)^(p-n) delta^p, so K(z,s) <= (s/rho)^(alpha') delta <= delta. In particular integral_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p dmu < infinity.

subproblem.title: Tilt-excess bounded by height with an L^1 mean-curvature term (Lemma A)
subproblem.statement: For n >= 1 and l >= 0 there is a constant C >= 0 (one may take C = 144) such that: if U is open, V is a rectifiable n-varifold in U with generalized mean curvature H in U, z in R^(n+l), r > 0, h >= 0, B_r(z) contained in U, T an n-dimensional subspace, and dist(x - z, T) <= h for every x in spt V cap B_r(z), then integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= C r^-2 integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + C h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu (Bochner integrals with respect to mu = V.weight; |.| Hilbert-Schmidt; p_x = V.tangentProj x; balls closed).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Lemma A of the parent proof (the L^1 form of the computation proving Simon Ch. 5, Lemma 2.1), with a general cut-off so that the constant is an absolute number C (C = 144 when |phi'| <= 3).

Notation. mu := V.weight, spt V := V.support, p_x := V.tangentProj x, p_T := T.starProjection, |A| the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (|A|^2 = hsNormSq A = trace(A^* A)), ||A|| the operator norm (||A|| <= |A|), x' := p_{T^perp}(x - z), so |x'| = dist(x - z, T) = infDist (x - z) T.
Facts used. (T) [sibling allard52_tangent_ae] p is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, and for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace. (F2) mu(K) < infinity for compact K in U (theta is integrable on M cap K); mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0 and mu(R^(n+l) minus U) = 0, so mu-a.e. point lies in spt V.

1. Cut-off and constant. Fix phi in C^infinity(R, [0,1]) with phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1/2] and phi = 0 on [1, infinity) (for instance a mollified piecewise linear function, which can be chosen with |phi'| <= 3), let c_phi := sup|phi'| < infinity and C := max{16 c_phi^2, 4} (C = 144 if c_phi = 3). C is an absolute constant. Given z, r, h, T as in the statement put zeta(x) := phi(|x - z|/r). Since phi is constant near 0, zeta is C^infinity; 0 <= zeta <= 1, zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), zeta = 0 outside the open ball B^o_r(z), and |grad zeta| <= c_phi / r.

2. Test field. X(x) := zeta(x)^2 x' = zeta(x)^2 p_{T^perp}(x - z). X is C^infinity, tsupport X is contained in B_r(z), which is a compact subset of U, so X is admissible in V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H: integral div_M X dmu = -integral X.H dmu, where div_M X(x) = V.divM X x = trace(DX(x) o p_x). (X.H is integrable since H is in L^1_loc(mu) on U and X is bounded with compact support in U.)

3. Divergence. DX(x)v = zeta^2 p_{T^perp} v + 2 zeta (grad zeta . v) x'. At mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace (T); there trace(DX o p_x) = zeta^2 trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) + 2 zeta grad zeta . p_x x' (the trace of v -> (a . p_x v) b is a . p_x b). For two rank-n orthogonal projections, |p_x - p_T|^2 = trace((p_x - p_T)^2) = 2n - 2 trace(p_T p_x), so trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) = n - trace(p_T p_x) = (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2 =: s(x); and p_T x' = 0 gives p_x x' = (p_x - p_T)x'. 4. Integrability. All functions involved are bounded (|p_x - p_T|^2 <= (|p_x| + |p_T|)^2 <= 4n since p_x is 0 or a rank-n projection), mu-a.e. strongly measurable by (T), and vanish outside B_r(z), which has finite mu-measure by (F2). Hence they are mu-integrable, and the first variation identity becomes
 integral zeta^2 s dmu = -integral 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' dmu - integral zeta^2 x' . H dmu.

5. Absorption. |(p_x - p_T) x'| <= ||p_x - p_T|| |x'| <= |p_x - p_T| |x'| = sqrt(2s) |x'|, and with a := zeta sqrt(s), b := |grad zeta| |x'| we have 2 sqrt(2) a b <= a^2/2 + 4 b^2 (as (a/sqrt 2 - 2b)^2 >= 0). Hence |2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T)x'| <= (1/2) zeta^2 s + 4 |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2, and |zeta^2 x'.H| <= zeta^2 |x'| |H|. So integral zeta^2 s <= (1/2) integral zeta^2 s + 4 integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 + integral zeta^2 |x'| |H|, and since integral zeta^2 s < infinity,
 integral zeta^2 s dmu <= 8 integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 dmu + 2 integral zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu.

6. Conclusion. As zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z) and s >= 0, (1/2) integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= integral zeta^2 s dmu. As |grad zeta|^2 <= c_phi^2 r^-2 and grad zeta, zeta vanish outside B_r(z), integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 dmu <= c_phi^2 r^-2 integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu. mu-a.e. x in B_r(z) lies in spt V cap B_r(z) (F2) and therefore satisfies |x'| = dist(x - z, T) <= h by hypothesis, so integral zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu <= h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu. Therefore
 integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 16 c_phi^2 r^-2 integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu <= C (r^2)^-1 integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + C h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu.
 All integrals here are Bochner integrals of integrable functions: the left integrand by step 4, dist(x - z, T)^2 is continuous and bounded on the compact set B_r(z) of finite measure, and |H| is integrable on B_r(z) because H is in L^1_loc(mu) on U (V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H) and B_r(z) is a compact subset of U. This is the asserted inequality with the constant C, which depends on nothing.

div_M X = zeta^2 (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2 + 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' at mu-a.e. x
First variation identity with bounded integrable terms
Absorb the cross term by AM-GM
Use zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), |grad zeta| <= c/r, and |x'| <= h at mu-a.e. point of B_r(z)

subproblem.title: Iteration of the tilt-excess decay theorem: limit planes with decay at all scales (Part I)
subproblem.statement: Assume TiltExcessDecayTheorem. For n >= 1, l >= 0 and p > n there are delta_1 > 0 and C >= 0 (depending only on n, l, p) such that: if U is open, V has generalized mean curvature H in U, 0 < delta <= delta_1, 2.3 holds (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho), xi in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0), sigma in (0, delta rho/2] and S_0 is an n-dimensional subspace, then there is an n-dimensional subspace S with |p_S - p_{S_0}|^2 <= C E_*(xi, sigma, S_0) and E(xi, s, S) <= C (s/sigma)^(2(1-n/p)) E_*(xi, sigma, S_0) for every s in (0, sigma], where E = V.tiltExcess, E_* = V.tiltExcessStar H p delta and |.| is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: TiltExcessDecayTheorem → ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∃ δ₁ C : ℝ, 0 < δ₁ ∧ 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ δ₁ → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → ∀ ξ ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall 0 (δ * ρ), ∀ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ → σ ≤ δ * ρ / 2 → ∀ S₀ : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ S₀ = n → ∃ S : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ S = n ∧ hsNormSq (S.starProjection - S₀.starProjection) ≤ C * V.tiltExcessStar H p δ ξ σ S₀ ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ σ → V.tiltExcess ξ s S ≤ C * (s / σ) ^ (2 * (1 - n / p)) * V.tiltExcessStar H p δ ξ σ S₀
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Part I of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 5, proof of 5.2, steps (1)-(7), and Remark 4.6), with the parameter delta of 2.3 in place of the parent's delta_1.

Notation. mu := V.weight, p_x := V.tangentProj x, p_S := S.starProjection, |.| the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm), omega_n := unitBallVolume n, alpha' := 1 - n/p in (0,1); E(xi, s, T) := V.tiltExcess xi s T = s^-n integral_{B_s(xi)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu; E_*(xi, s, T) := V.tiltExcessStar H p delta xi s T = max{E(xi,s,T), delta^-1 K(xi,s)^2}, K := V.scaledLpNorm H p (as a real number via toReal).
Hypotheses and facts used. (D) TiltExcessDecayTheorem (hypothesis of this theorem): for n, l, p there are eta, delta_45 in (0, 1/4] such that, if 2.3 holds with delta in (0, delta_45], sigma in (0, delta rho/2], xi in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0) and dim T = n, then E_*(xi, eta sigma, S) <= eta^(2 alpha') E_*(xi, sigma, T) for some n-dimensional S. (P) [sibling allard52_density_bounds, applied to the given n, p and then to the given l] there are delta_P in (0, 1/8], C_P > 0 with C_P delta_P <= 1/2 (depending only on n and p) such that under 2.3 with delta <= delta_P, |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2: mu(B_s(y)) <= (1 + C_P delta) omega_n s^n <= 2 omega_n s^n, and if y in spt V also mu(B_s(y)) >= (1 - C_P delta) omega_n s^n >= omega_n s^n / 2. (T) [sibling allard52_tangent_ae] p is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, and for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace; by the definition of V.tangentProj, p_x is in any case either 0 or such a projection.
Constants. delta_1 := min{delta_45, delta_P} > 0, C_II := (8/omega_n) eta^-n (1 - eta^(alpha'))^-2, C_III := (2 eta^-n + 4 omega_n C_II) eta^(-2 alpha'), C := max{C_II, C_III} >= 0; all depend only on n, l, p.

Let 0 < delta <= delta_1, assume 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho), xi in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0), sigma in (0, delta rho/2], and S_0 n-dimensional. Put E_*^(0) := E_*(xi, sigma, S_0).

1. Integrability. For every B_s(z) contained in B_rho(0) (in particular B_s(xi) with s <= sigma, since |xi| + s <= delta rho + delta rho/2 < rho) and every n-dimensional T, the function x -> |p_x - p_T|^2 is bounded by 4n (p_x is 0 or a rank-n orthogonal projection, |p_T|^2 = n), mu-a.e. strongly measurable by (T), and mu(B_s(z)) < infinity (B_s(z) is a compact subset of U). So it is mu-integrable on B_s(z); E(z, s, T) is a genuine integral, E <= E_*, and s'^n E(z, s', T) <= s^n E(z, s, T) for s' <= s (integral of a nonnegative integrable function over a smaller set).

2. Iteration of 4.5 (book (1)). Define S_j recursively: given S_{j-1} (dim n), apply (D) with sigma_j := eta^(j-1) sigma (in (0, delta rho/2]) and T := S_{j-1} to obtain S_j (dim n) with E_*(xi, eta^j sigma, S_j) <= eta^(2 alpha') E_*(xi, eta^(j-1) sigma, S_{j-1}). By induction E_*(xi, eta^j sigma, S_j) <= eta^(2 alpha' j) E_*^(0) for all j >= 0.

3. Consecutive planes (book (3), Remark 4.6). Let j >= 1 and B := B_{eta^j sigma}(xi). Since xi in spt V, |xi| <= delta rho <= 3 delta rho and eta^j sigma <= rho/2, (P) gives mu(B) >= omega_n (eta^j sigma)^n / 2. Integrating |p_{S_j} - p_{S_{j-1}}|^2 <= 2|p_x - p_{S_j}|^2 + 2|p_x - p_{S_{j-1}}|^2 over B and using step 1,
 mu(B) |p_{S_j} - p_{S_{j-1}}|^2 <= 2 (eta^j sigma)^n E(xi, eta^j sigma, S_j) + 2 (eta^(j-1) sigma)^n E(xi, eta^(j-1) sigma, S_{j-1}),
 hence, by step 2 and E <= E_*, |p_{S_j} - p_{S_{j-1}}|^2 <= (4/omega_n)[eta^(2 alpha' j) + eta^-n eta^(2 alpha'(j-1))] E_*^(0) <= (8/omega_n) eta^-n eta^(2 alpha'(j-1)) E_*^(0).

4. Limit plane (book (4)-(6)). By step 3, |p_{S_j} - p_{S_{j-1}}| <= a eta^(alpha'(j-1)) with a := ((8/omega_n) eta^-n E_*^(0))^(1/2). Hence (p_{S_j}) is a Cauchy sequence in the finite-dimensional space of operators and converges to some P_infinity, with |P_infinity - p_{S_k}| <= sum_{j>k} a eta^(alpha'(j-1)) = a eta^(alpha' k)/(1 - eta^(alpha')), i.e.
 (5) |P_infinity - p_{S_k}|^2 <= C_II eta^(2 alpha' k) E_*^(0) for k >= 0.
 The set of orthogonal projections of rank n, {P : P^2 = P, P^* = P, trace P = n}, is closed, so P_infinity = p_S for the n-dimensional subspace S := range P_infinity. With k = 0: hsNormSq(p_S - p_{S_0}) <= C_II E_*^(0) <= C E_*^(0).

5. Decay at all scales (book (7)). Let 0 < s <= sigma and choose j >= 0 with eta^(j+1) sigma < s <= eta^j sigma. Integrating |p_x - p_S|^2 <= 2|p_x - p_{S_j}|^2 + 2|p_{S_j} - p_S|^2 over B_s(xi) contained in B_{eta^j sigma}(xi), and using step 1, (P) (mu(B_s(xi)) <= 2 omega_n s^n), step 2 and (5):
 E(xi, s, S) <= 2 s^-n (eta^j sigma)^n E(xi, eta^j sigma, S_j) + 2 s^-n mu(B_s(xi)) |p_{S_j} - p_S|^2 <= 2 eta^-n eta^(2 alpha' j) E_*^(0) + 4 omega_n C_II eta^(2 alpha' j) E_*^(0),
 because eta^j sigma / s < eta^-1. Since eta^(j+1) < s/sigma, eta^(2 alpha' j) = eta^(-2 alpha') (eta^(j+1))^(2 alpha') <= eta^(-2 alpha') (s/sigma)^(2 alpha'). Hence E(xi, s, S) <= C_III (s/sigma)^(2 alpha') E_*^(0) <= C (s/sigma)^(2(1 - n/p)) E_*^(0).

Steps 4 and 5 give an n-dimensional S with hsNormSq(S.starProjection - S_0.starProjection) <= C E_*(xi, sigma, S_0) and V.tiltExcess xi s S <= C (s/sigma)^(2(1-n/p)) E_*(xi, sigma, S_0) for all 0 < s <= sigma, with delta_1 > 0 and C >= 0 depending only on n, l, p.
proof_key_steps: Tilt integrands are bounded and a.e. measurable, so tilt-excess is a genuine integral
Iterate 4.5 at radii eta^j sigma: E_*(xi, eta^j sigma, S_j) <= eta^(2 alpha' j) E_*^(0)
Density lower bound gives |p_{S_j} - p_{S_{j-1}}|^2 <= (8/omega_n) eta^-n eta^(2 alpha'(j-1)) E_*^(0)
Geometric series: p_{S_j} -> p_S with |p_S - p_{S_k}|^2 <= C_II eta^(2 alpha' k) E_*^(0)
Interpolate scales with the density upper bound: E(xi, s, S) <= C_III (s/sigma)^(2 alpha') E_*^(0)

audit.reason: TiltExcessDecayTheorem is an explicit hypothesis. Finite measurable tilt integrals, density bounds, geometric-series convergence of projections and interpolation between scales prove the exact limit-plane estimates using only the declared dependencies.

subproblem.statement: For n >= 1 and p > n there is delta_2 > 0, depending only on n and p (the same for every codimension l >= 0), such that: for every l >= 0, if U is open in R^(n+l), V has generalized mean curvature H in U, 0 < delta <= delta_2, 2.3 holds (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho), q is a linear isometry of R^(n+l), f : R^n -> R^l, 0 < R <= delta rho, f(0) = 0, f is 1-Lipschitz on B^n_R(0) and spt V cap B_R(0) = q(graph f over B^n_R(0)) cap B_R(0), then for every jointly Borel Phi : R^(n+l) x L(R^(n+l)) -> [0, infinity] and every measurable A contained in the open ball B^o_{R/2}(0) of R^n: integral_A Phi(F(x), P_q(Df(x))) dL^n(x) <= integral_{F(A)} Phi(w, p_w) dmu(w), where F(x) = q(graphPoint x (f x)), Df(x) = fderiv f x, P_q(B) is the orthogonal projection onto q(graph B) = (span{graphPoint v (B v)}).map q, p_w = V.tangentProj w and mu = V.weight.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(a)-(b) of the parent proof ('measure on the graph' via (M.iv), (UD), (F2); 'tangent planes' via (F1) and (Area)), stated as a single comparison inequality; the tangent-plane identification along the Lipschitz graph is proved directly by blowing up through the area formula.

Notation. mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult), spt V := V.support, p_w := V.tangentProj w, omega_n := unitBallVolume n. Given q, f, R as in the statement: F(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)) for x in R^n; Gamma_R := q '' graphOver f (B^n_R(0)); for a linear map A : R^n -> R^l, Pi_q(A) := starProjection of (span{graphPoint v (A v)}).map q, the orthogonal projection onto the n-plane q(graph A). Then the left integrand of the statement is Phi(F(x), Pi_q(Df(x))) with Df(x) := fderiv f x.
Facts used. (P.ii) [sibling allard52_density_bounds] for the given n and p there are delta_P in (0, 1/8] and C_P > 0 with C_P delta_P <= 1/2, depending only on n and p (the same for every codimension l), such that under 2.3 with delta <= delta_P, if y in spt V, |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2 then mu(B_s(y)) >= (1 - C_P delta) omega_n s^n >= omega_n s^n/2. (T) [sibling allard52_tangent_ae] p is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. (UD) [Simon Ch. 1, Thm 3.2(1); SimonGMT Chapter01.mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity] if nu is a Borel regular measure and Theta^{*n}(nu, x) >= t for every x in a set Z, then nu(Z) >= t H^n(Z). (Area) [Simon Ch. 2, Sect. 3; SimonGMT Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitz_simon] for an injective Lipschitz map G : R^n -> R^(n+l) and Borel g >= 0, integral_{G(A)} g dH^n = integral_A g(G(x)) J_G(x) dx; for an injective linear map the same holds with constant Jacobian. (Rad) Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt). (Leb) Lebesgue's differentiation theorem on R^n. (Cont) [sibling allard52_graph_plane_algebra, last conjunct] for each linear isometry q, the map B -> Pi_q(B) is continuous on the space of linear maps R^n -> R^l (directly: Pi_q(B) = q J_B (I + B^* B)^-1 J_B^* q^-1 with J_B v := graphPoint v (B v); each factor depends continuously on B and inversion is continuous on invertible operators).
Choice of constant; it depends only on n and p. Fix n >= 1 and p > n, and let delta_P, C_P be the constants of allard52_density_bounds for (n, p); they do not depend on l. Put delta_2 := delta_P, so 0 < delta_2 <= 1/8 and delta_2 depends only on n and p. Only now let l >= 0 be arbitrary. The steps below use delta only through delta <= delta_2 = delta_P (for (P.ii)) and delta <= 1/8; hence the same delta_2 works for every l, which is the statement with "there exists delta_2" placed before "for all l".

Let 0 < delta <= delta_2, 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho), q, f, R with 0 < R <= delta rho, f(0) = 0, f 1-Lipschitz on B^n_R(0) and spt V cap B_R(0) = Gamma_R cap B_R(0).

1. Elementary facts. For x, x' in B^n_R(0): |F(x) - F(x')|^2 = |x - x'|^2 + |f(x) - f(x')|^2, so |x - x'| <= |F(x) - F(x')| <= sqrt 2 |x - x'|, and |F(x)| <= sqrt 2 |x| (f(0) = 0). F is injective on B^n_R(0), and its inverse on Gamma_R is the restriction of the 1-Lipschitz linear map a(w) := first n coordinates of q^-1 w; hence F maps L^n-null subsets of B^n_R(0) to H^n-null sets and a maps H^n-null subsets of Gamma_R to L^n-null sets. If x in B^o_{R/2}(0) then |F(x)| < R, so F(x) in Gamma_R cap B_R(0) = spt V cap B_R(0); thus F(B^o_{R/2}(0)) is contained in spt V cap B^o_R(0), and B_R(0) is contained in B_rho(0) (R <= delta rho <= rho/8), which is contained in U by 2.3.

2. Differentiability. Extend f restricted to B^n_R(0) to a Lipschitz map f~ : R^n -> R^l (componentwise McShane extension, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi; constant at most sqrt l); F~(x) := q(graphPoint x (f~ x)) is Lipschitz and injective on R^n. By (Rad), f is differentiable at L^n-a.e. x in B^o_R(0) (f = f~ near such x), and there DF(x)v = q(graphPoint v (Df(x)v)), DF(x)(R^n) = q(graph Df(x)) is n-dimensional, and J_F(x) = det(I + Df(x)^* Df(x))^(1/2) >= 1.

3. The carrier fills the graph. Let Z := (spt V cap B^o_R(0)) minus M. For y in Z we have |y| < R <= delta rho <= 3 delta rho, so by (P.ii) mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n s^n/2 for all s in (0, rho/2]; for s < R - |y| the ball B_s(y) lies in B^o_R(0), so the finite Radon measure nu := mu restricted to B^o_R(0) satisfies Theta^{*n}(nu, y) >= 1/2 on Z. Since mu(R^(n+l) minus M) = 0, nu(Z) = 0, and (UD) gives H^n(Z) <= 2 nu(Z) = 0. Also H^n(M minus spt V) = 0 (mu(M minus spt V) = 0 because spt mu has full measure, and theta > 0 on M). Since spt V cap B^o_R(0) = Gamma_R cap B^o_R(0), the sets M cap B^o_R(0) and Gamma_R cap B^o_R(0) differ by an H^n-null set.

4. Multiplicity at least 1. N := {w in M : theta(w) < 1} satisfies mu(N) = integral_N theta dH^n = 0 by 2.3 (theta >= 1 mu-a.e.); as theta > 0 on N, H^n(N) = 0. Thus theta >= 1 H^n-a.e. on M.

5. Tangent planes along the graph. Claim: for L^n-a.e. x in B^o_{R/2}(0), if F(x) in M then f is differentiable at x and p_{F(x)} = Pi_q(Df(x)).
 Let theta~ := theta on M and theta~ := 1 off M, and g(x) := theta~(F(x)) J_F(x) on B^o_R(0). For compact K' contained in B^o_R(0), F(K') is compact and contained in B_{sqrt2 R}(0), which lies in B_rho(0) and hence in U (sqrt 2 R <= sqrt 2 delta rho < rho, as delta <= delta_2 <= 1/8), and by (Area) integral_{K'} g dx = integral_{F(K')} theta~ dH^n <= integral_{F(K') cap M} theta dH^n + H^n(F(K')) < infinity (theta is integrable on M cap F(K'); H^n(F(K')) < infinity since F is Lipschitz). Since theta is H^n-a.e.-measurable on M and a maps H^n-null sets to L^n-null sets, g is L^1_loc on B^o_R(0). Exclude the L^n-null set of x in B^o_{R/2}(0) at which f is not differentiable or x is not a Lebesgue point of g with value g(x) (Leb). Let x be any remaining point with y := F(x) in M, and let psi in C_c(R^(n+l)) with spt psi in B_rho'(0). For 0 < r < (R - |y|)/rho', the ball B_{r rho'}(y) lies in B^o_R(0), where M and Gamma_R agree up to H^n-null sets (step 3), so by the blow-up identity (H^n(y + r E) = r^n H^n(E)) and (Area) applied to F,
 integral_{eta_{y,r}(M)} psi(z) theta(y + r z) dH^n(z) = r^-n integral_M psi((w - y)/r) theta(w) dH^n(w) = r^-n integral_{Gamma_R} psi((w - y)/r) theta~(w) dH^n(w) = r^-n integral_{B^o_R(0)} psi((F(x') - F(x))/r) g(x') dx' = integral_{R^n} psi((F(x + r v) - F(x))/r) g(x + r v) dv,
 where the last integrand vanishes unless |v| <= rho' (because |F(x + r v) - F(x)| >= r|v|). As r -> 0, (F(x + r v) - F(x))/r -> DF(x)v uniformly for |v| <= rho' (differentiability), so psi((F(x + r v) - F(x))/r) -> psi(DF(x)v) uniformly there (psi is uniformly continuous and bounded), and integral_{B_rho'(0)} |g(x + r v) - g(x)| dv -> 0 (Lebesgue point). Hence the integral tends to g(x) integral psi(DF(x)v) dv = theta(y) J_F(x) integral psi(DF(x)v) dv = theta(y) integral_{q(graph Df(x))} psi dH^n by (Area) for the injective linear map DF(x). So the n-dimensional subspace q(graph Df(x)) is the approximate tangent space of M w.r.t. theta at y (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7 = HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt). As theta(y) > 0 it is unique (SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so by the definition of V.tangentProj, p_y = Pi_q(Df(x)). This proves the claim.

6. Conclusion. Let Phi be jointly Borel, A a measurable subset of B^o_{R/2}(0). By step 1 F(A) is contained in spt V cap B^o_R(0). The set of x in A with F(x) not in M is mapped by F into Z, an H^n-null set (step 3), so it is L^n-null (a is Lipschitz). With steps 2 and 5, for L^n-a.e. x in A: F(x) in M, f is differentiable at x, J_F(x) >= 1 and p_{F(x)} = Pi_q(Df(x)). Therefore, using J_F >= 1, (Area) for the injective Lipschitz map F~ on A (F~ = F on A, with the same Jacobian at differentiability points of the open ball), step 3 (H^n(F(A) minus M) = 0), step 4 (theta >= 1 H^n-a.e. on M) and mu = theta H^n restricted to M:

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(b)-(e) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 5, proof of 5.2, (10)-(11) and the Hoelder argument after (11)), with abstract decay data. The Lebesgue-point step is done in the parameter domain R^n, and the identification of planes is extended to every point by continuity, as in the parent's step 4(e).

Notation. mu := V.weight, spt V := V.support, p_w := V.tangentProj w, p_S := S.starProjection, |.| the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNorm), ||.|| the operator norm, omega_n := unitBallVolume n, alpha' := 1 - n/p in (0,1). Given q, f: F(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)); for a linear map B : R^n -> R^l, Pi_q(B) := orthogonal projection onto (span{graphPoint v (B v)}).map q (the plane q(graph B)); Df(x) := fderiv f x; G(x) := Pi_q(Df(x)). E(z, s, T) := V.tiltExcess z s T = s^-n integral_{B_s(z)} |p_w - p_T|^2 dmu (Bochner integral). Balls B_s(z) are closed, B^o open.
Facts used.
 (Alg) [sibling allard52_graph_plane_algebra, for the given n, l] there is L_0 = L_0(n,l) in (0, 1/4] such that: |B_1 - B_2|^2 <= |Pi_q(B_1) - Pi_q(B_2)|^2 <= 3|B_1 - B_2|^2 whenever |B_1|, |B_2| <= L_0; ||B|| <= |B| <= sqrt(n) ||B||; B -> Pi_q(B) is continuous.
 (Cmp) [sibling allard52_graph_comparison, for the given n, p and then the given l] there is delta_2 > 0 such that under 2.3 with delta <= delta_2, for q, f, R with 0 < R <= delta rho, f(0) = 0, f 1-Lipschitz on B^n_R(0) and spt V cap B_R(0) = q '' graphOver f (B^n_R(0)) cap B_R(0), every jointly Borel Phi >= 0 and every measurable A contained in B^o_{R/2}(0): integral_A Phi(F(x), G(x)) dx <= integral_{F(A)} Phi(w, p_w) dmu(w). Only delta_2 > 0 is known about delta_2.
 (T) [sibling allard52_tangent_ae] p is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. By the definition of V.tangentProj (whose planes have dimension n), p_w is, for every w, either 0 or the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace; hence |p_w - p_T|^2 <= (|p_w| + |p_T|)^2 <= 4n for every n-dimensional T.
 (Fin) [contract field V.integrableOn_mult] theta is H^n-integrable on M cap K for every compact K contained in U, so mu(K) < infinity for such K.
 (Leb) Lebesgue's differentiation theorem on R^n; (Rad) Rademacher's theorem.
Constants. L := L_0/sqrt(n) (so 0 < L <= 1/4), delta_3 := min{delta_2, 1/8} (so 0 < delta_3 <= 1/8 and delta_3 <= delta_2), C := (2^(2n+4)/omega_n)^(1/2) >= 0. They depend only on n, l, p.

Let 0 < delta <= delta_3, 2.3 (AllardHypotheses H p delta rho), q, f, R with 0 < R <= delta rho, f(0) = 0, Lip f <= L on B^n_R(0), spt V cap B_R(0) = q '' graphOver f (B^n_R(0)) cap B_R(0), and S, A >= 0 with dim S(zeta) = n and E(zeta, s, S(zeta)) <= A (s/R)^(2 alpha') for zeta in spt V cap B_{R/2}(0) and 0 < s <= R/2.

1. Preliminaries. Since delta <= delta_3 <= 1/8 and 0 < R <= delta rho, we have R <= rho/8 < rho; hence B_R(0) is contained in B_rho(0), which is contained in U by 2.3 (closedBall 0 rho is contained in U). Since delta <= delta_3 <= delta_2, (Cmp) is available. For x, x' in B^n_R(0), |F(x) - F(x')| <= (1 + L^2)^(1/2) |x - x'| <= 2|x - x'| and |F(x)| <= 2|x|. By (Rad) (applied to a Lipschitz extension), f is differentiable at L^n-a.e. x in B^o_R(0), with ||Df(x)|| <= L and hence |Df(x)| <= sqrt(n) L = L_0 (Alg). G is Borel (fderiv is Borel measurable, Pi_q continuous) and |G(x)|^2 = n. f is 1-Lipschitz on B^n_R(0) (L <= 1), so (Cmp) applies to (q, f, R).

2. Campanato inequality in the parameter domain (book (10)-(11)). Fix z in B^n_{R/4}(0) and 0 < s <= R/4, and put zeta := F(z), Q := S(zeta). Since |zeta| <= 2|z| <= R/2 and zeta in q '' graphOver f (B^n_R(0)) cap B_R(0) = spt V cap B_R(0), zeta lies in spt V cap B_{R/2}(0), so dim Q = n and E(zeta, s, Q) <= A (s/R)^(2 alpha'). Apply (Cmp) with A_z := B^n_{s/2}(z) (measurable and contained in B^o_{R/2}(0), as |z| + s/2 <= 3R/8) and Phi(w, P) := 1_{B_s(zeta)}(w) ofReal(|P - p_Q|^2) (jointly Borel). For x' in A_z, |F(x') - zeta| <= 2 (s/2) = s, so the indicator equals 1 along F(A_z), and
 integral_{B^n_{s/2}(z)} ofReal(|G(x') - p_Q|^2) dx' <= integral_{F(A_z)} 1_{B_s(zeta)} ofReal(|p_w - p_Q|^2) dmu <= integral_{B_s(zeta)} ofReal(|p_w - p_Q|^2) dmu.
 Containment and finiteness: every w in B_s(zeta) has |w| <= |zeta| + s <= R/2 + R/4 < R <= rho/8, so B_s(zeta) is contained in B_R(0), hence in B_rho(0) and in U (step 1). Thus B_s(zeta) is a compact subset of U and mu(B_s(zeta)) < infinity by (Fin). The function w -> |p_w - p_Q|^2 is bounded by 4n and mu-a.e. strongly measurable (T), so it is mu-integrable on B_s(zeta), and the lintegral of its ofReal equals ofReal of its Bochner integral:
 integral_{B_s(zeta)} ofReal(|p_w - p_Q|^2) dmu = ofReal(integral_{B_s(zeta)} |p_w - p_Q|^2 dmu) = ofReal(s^n E(zeta, s, Q)) <= ofReal(A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha')).
 Since G is bounded and Borel, the left side is ofReal of the corresponding Bochner integral. Thus, with c(z) := p_{S(F(z))}:
 (C) integral_{B^n_{s/2}(z)} |G(x') - c(z)|^2 dx' <= A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha') for all z in B^n_{R/4}(0), 0 < s <= R/4.

3. Identification almost everywhere. G is bounded and Borel, so by (Leb), for L^n-a.e. z in B^o_{R/4}(0), the mean of |G - G(z)|^2 over B^n_t(z) tends to 0 as t -> 0. At such z, with t = s/2, |G(z) - c(z)|^2 <= 2 (mean of |G - G(z)|^2 over B^n_{s/2}(z)) + 2 (mean of |G - c(z)|^2 over B^n_{s/2}(z)) <= o(1) + 2 (omega_n (s/2)^n)^-1 A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha') -> 0 as s -> 0. Hence (I) G(z) = c(z) for L^n-a.e. z in B^o_{R/4}(0).

4. Hoelder estimate for almost every pair (book, after (11)). Let Z be the set of z in B^o_{R/16}(0) at which f is differentiable and (I) holds; its complement in the ball is L^n-null. Let x_1 != x_2 in Z, d := |x_1 - x_2| < R/8, m := (x_1 + x_2)/2. Then B^n_{d/2}(m) is contained in B^n_d(x_1) cap B^n_d(x_2). For x' in B^n_{d/2}(m), |c(x_1) - c(x_2)|^2 <= 2|G(x') - c(x_1)|^2 + 2|G(x') - c(x_2)|^2; averaging over B^n_{d/2}(m) and applying (C) with s = 2d (<= R/4) at z = x_1 and z = x_2 (B^n_{s/2}(x_i) = B^n_d(x_i)):
 |c(x_1) - c(x_2)|^2 <= (2/(omega_n (d/2)^n)) 2 A (2d)^n (2d/R)^(2 alpha') = (2^(2n+2+2 alpha')/omega_n) A (d/R)^(2 alpha') <= C^2 A (d/R)^(2 alpha').
 By (I), G(x_i) = c(x_i), and by (Alg) (|Df(x_i)| <= L_0): |Df(x_1) - Df(x_2)|^2 <= |G(x_1) - G(x_2)|^2 = |c(x_1) - c(x_2)|^2. Hence
 (H) |Df(x_1) - Df(x_2)| <= C sqrt(A) (|x_1 - x_2|/R)^(alpha') for all x_1, x_2 in Z.

5. f is C^1 (Rad, as in the parent's step 4(d)). By (H), Df restricted to Z is uniformly continuous, and Z is dense in B^o_{R/16}(0) (full measure); let g be the unique continuous map on B^o_{R/16}(0) with g = Df on Z; g satisfies (H) on the whole ball. For x in the ball and h with x + [0,1]h in the ball: for L^n-a.e. y near x the segment y + [0,1]h meets the complement of Z in a set of 1-dimensional measure zero (Fubini), and f(y + h) - f(y) = integral_0^1 Df(y + t h) h dt = integral_0^1 g(y + t h) h dt (f is Lipschitz, hence absolutely continuous along segments). Both sides are continuous in y, so f(x + h) - f(x) = integral_0^1 g(x + t h) h dt for every such x, h. Therefore |f(x + h) - f(x) - g(x)h| <= sup_{t in [0,1]} ||g(x + t h) - g(x)|| |h| = o(|h|): f is differentiable at every point of B^o_{R/16}(0) with fderiv f = g, which is continuous. So f is C^1 on the open ball B^o_{R/16}(0) (ContDiffOn R 1 f (ball 0 (R/16))), and (H) holds for all x, y in that ball: hsNorm(fderiv f x - fderiv f y) <= C sqrt(A) (|x - y|/R)^(1 - n/p).

6. Identification of planes at every point (parent's step 4(e)). Let z in B^o_{R/16}(0) and let s in (0, R/4] be so small that B^n_{s/2}(z) is contained in B^o_{R/16}(0). For x' in B^n_{s/2}(z), (Alg) and (H) give |G(x') - G(z)|^2 <= 3|Df(x') - Df(z)|^2 <= 3 C^2 A (s/(2R))^(2 alpha') (|Df| <= L_0 at every point of the ball, since f is L-Lipschitz there). Then |G(z) - c(z)|^2 <= 2|G(x') - G(z)|^2 + 2|G(x') - c(z)|^2; averaging over B^n_{s/2}(z) and using (C),
 |G(z) - c(z)|^2 <= 6 C^2 A (s/(2R))^(2 alpha') + 2 (omega_n (s/2)^n)^-1 A s^n (s/R)^(2 alpha') -> 0 as s -> 0.
 Hence Pi_q(Df(z)) = p_{S(F(z))}. Two subspaces with the same orthogonal projection coincide (each is the range of its projection, Mathlib Submodule.range_starProjection), so (span{graphPoint v (fderiv f z v)}).map q = S(q(graphPoint z (f z))) for every z in B^o_{R/16}(0).

Steps 5 and 6 give the three conclusions, with L, delta_3, C depending only on n, l, p.

Graph comparison plus B_s(zeta) in B_rho(0) (so finite mass and a bounded measurable integrand) turn the decay of E(F(z), s, S(F z)) into a Campanato bound for G = P_q(Df)
Lebesgue differentiation gives G(z) = p_{S(F z)} a.e.
Midpoint averaging and (Gp) give the Hoelder estimate for a.e. pairs
A Lipschitz map whose a.e. derivative has a continuous extension is C^1
Continuity of Df and the Campanato bound identify the planes at every point
